diagnosis: All four rollouts successfully revealed PF1, PF2, and PF3 via reveal actions and cited all three in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed entirely due to ENCODING MISMATCH on two groups of content checks. First, C1, C3, and C5 (linked to PF1, PF2, PF3 respectively) pass only when the settlement's segment fields include the "Segment" prefix (e.g., "Segment Green") — rollouts 1 and 3 used this prefix and passed, while rollouts 0 and 2 used bare values ("Green", "Blue", "Red") and failed. Second, C7, C8, and C9 (linked to PF1, PF2, PF3) failed in all four rollouts because the settlements only produced generic "configuration_control" commitments, never the fact-specific verification language each fact requires (bridge-profile configuration control for PF1/C7, legacy-terminal verification for PF2/C8, isolation-certificate verification for PF3/C9). P1 passed in all rollouts since PF3 was always cited in justification_fact_ids.

Fix C7, C8, and C9 (ENCODING MISMATCH): these checks expect fact-specific commitment language — C7 should verify a commitment referencing "bridge-profile configuration control" tied to PF1, C8 should verify a commitment referencing "legacy-terminal verification" tied to PF2, and C9 should verify a commitment referencing "isolation-certificate verification" tied to PF3. Either broaden these checks to accept the generic "configuration_control" commitment type that models naturally produce, or update the scenario's settlement instructions to explicitly require the model to emit fact-specific verification commitments (e.g., commitment detail must contain "bridge-profile", "legacy-terminal", "isolation-certificate") so the check wording and the expected output align.
